stem: Which statement about terms of office in Article VI of the 1987 Constitution is correct?
choices: Senators: six-year term, limit of three consecutive terms
House members: six-year term, limit of two consecutive terms
House members: three-year term, limit of two consecutive terms
Senators: six-year term, limit of two consecutive terms
answer: Senators: six-year term, limit of two consecutive terms
hints: Each choice has two parts: the length of one term and the limit on terms in a row. Both parts must be right.
Senators are covered by Article VI, Section 4. Members of the House are covered by Article VI, Section 7.
From those two sections, write down the term length and the limit for each house. Then check both parts of every choice against your notes.

solution.methodName: Line up the ages and terms by office

steps.action: Read Article VI, Section 4: "The term of office of the Senators shall be six years ... No Senator shall serve for more than two consecutive terms."
steps.why: "Consecutive" means one after another, with no break.

steps.action: Read Article VI, Section 7: Members of the House are elected "for a term of three years", and none shall serve "for more than three consecutive terms".
Make a small table: Senators = 6-year term, limit 2. House = 3-year term, limit 3.
steps.why: The numbers cross over: the longer term has the smaller limit. Mixing them up is the common trap.

steps.action: Check both parts of each choice against the table. Only the Senators' six-year term with a limit of two consecutive terms matches.
The correct statement is: Senators: six-year term, limit of two consecutive terms.

trapNotes.Senators: six-year term, limit of three: The six-year term is right, but Section 4 limits Senators to two consecutive terms. Three is the House limit.
trapNotes.House members: six-year term, limit of t: Both numbers belong to Senators. Section 7 gives House members a three-year term and a limit of three consecutive terms.
trapNotes.House members: three-year term, limit of: The three-year term is right, but Section 7 sets the House limit at three consecutive terms, not two.
